subject.title: fix(openai): enable prompt cache keys for Azure

question: Should OpenClaw accept Azure Chat Completions as prompt-cache-key capable by default after rebasing this PR onto the current `packages/ai` provider path?
rationale: The code shape is coherent and supported by live proof, but it changes default request payload fields for existing Azure routes and the submitted branch is now conflict-dirty against current main.

options.title: Rebase and land Azure default
options.body: Carry the PR onto current main, keep `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey: false` as the opt-out, rerun focused provider/transport tests, and accept the Azure default behavior.

options.title: Keep explicit compat only
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers prefer Azure Chat Completions users to keep setting `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey` explicitly despite the upstream support proof.

options.title: Narrow detection before merge
options.body: Require a smaller host/provider allowlist or additional Azure deployment proof before auto-emitting cache fields on all detected Azure Chat Completions routes.

recommendation.title: Rebase and land Azure default
recommendation.body: Carry the PR onto current main, keep `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey: false` as the opt-out, rerun focused provider/transport tests, and accept the Azure default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current explicit-compat completions cache-key behavior landed through steipete's commit, so this default-behavior expansion is closest to that ownership trail.
